;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**[[United Nations]] [[Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights|High Commissioner for Human Rights]] [[Zeid Ra’ad Al Hussein]] asks [[Israel]] to refrain from using lethal force as protests enter their fifth week. The [[Israeli Defence Forces]] open fire again, including use of live ammunition. [https://www.haaretz.com/middle-east-news/palestinians/fifth-week-of-gaza-march-of-return-protests-to-begin-1.6033006 (Haaretz)] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/un-rights-official-to-israel-avoid-excessive-force-in-gaza/2018/04/27/c7773740-4a01-11e8-8082-105a446d19b8_story.html?noredirect=on&utm_term=.773a73a3ba11 (''The Washington Post'')] 
**Three Palestinians are killed and over 300 hurt according to the [[Hamas]]-run health ministry as thousands protested. The [[Israeli Defence Forces|Israeli army]] says that hundreds of rioters tried to infiltrate Israel, attempted to start fires in a number of ways, and attacked the security fence with explosive devices, grenades, and rocks. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/25-said-hurt-in-latest-gaza-riots-as-un-condemns-israels-excessive-force/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**Protestors give thanks to actress [[Natalie Portman]], who last week drew criticism from [[Israel]] after refusing to accept the [[Genesis Prize]] from [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Binyamin Netanyahu]]. [http://www.israelnationalnews.com/News/News.aspx/245102 (Arutz Sheva)]
*[[2018 Nicaraguan protests]]
**The [[Nicaragua]]n Centre for [[Human Rights]] says the death toll from ongoing anti-government protests has reached 38. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/27/americas/nicaragua-unrest/index.html (CNN)]
;Arts and culture
*[[LGBT rights in Kenya]]
**The [[Kenya]] [[Kenya Film Classification Board|Film Classification Board]] bans the [[lesbian]] [[romance film]] ''Rafiki'' saying it intends to "promote lesbianism". [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/27/africa/kenya-bans-lesbian-movie-ahead-cannes/index.html (CNN)]
;Business and economy
*Conservative media site [[RedState]] fires most of its staff and its owner [[Salem Media Group]] freezes the site, stating they could "no longer support the entire roster of writers and editors". Staff claim they were fired for their opposition to [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]. [http://thehill.com/homenews/media/385207-trump-critics-fired-at-conservative-site-redstate (''The Hill'')]
;Disasters and accidents
*[[Southwest Airlines Flight 1380]]
**[[Jet engine]] manufacturer [[CFM International]] calls for heightened checks of its [[CFM56-7B]] after a [[Boeing 737]] passenger died in an accident this month. The CFM56-7B is one of the most commonly used engines worldwide. [https://www.cnbc.com/2018/04/26/southwest-not-just-looking-at-fan-blades-in-fatal-mid-air-failure.html (CNBC)]
*The death toll from [[flash flood]]s in the [[Dead Sea]], [[Israel]], reaches fourteen including ten teenage hikers with a lorry driver still missing. Three youth workers connected to the hike are arrested. Two [[State of Palestine|Palestinian]] children are reported to have also died in the [[West Bank]]. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/nine-teenage-victims-of-dead-sea-flash-floods-named-1.6032911 (Haaretz)] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/middle_east/israeli-youth-leaders-arrested-for-negligence-after-floods-kill-10-hiking-teenagers/2018/04/27/1dec4464-4a00-11e8-9072-f6d4bc32f223_story.html?utm_term=.6a920e65119a (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[LaMia Flight 2933]]
**[[Colombia]]n investigators release their final report on the 2016 disaster, which killed 71 including most of the [[Associação Chapecoense de Futebol]] team. The report blames mismanagement leading to [[fuel exhaustion]], noting the aircraft departed without adequate fuel. [http://avherald.com/h?article=4a16583c/0017&opt=0 (The Aviation Herald)]
*The roof of a partially-constructed building collapses in [[Lahore]], [[Pakistan]]. Three are killed and two more injured. [https://nation.com.pk/28-Apr-2018/592159 (The Nation)]
*A [[Botswana Defence Force Air Wing|Botswanan]] [[Canadair CF-5|CF-5]] [[fighter jet]] crashes in [[Gaborone]], killing the pilot. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-04/28/c_137142375.htm (Xinhua)]
*[[Disasters in Indonesia]]
**[[2018 Balikpapan oil spill]]
***The [[China|Chinese]] captain of MV ''Ever Juder'' is charged in connection with an oil pipeline rupture and fire that killed five. He and 21 of his crew are detained in [[Balikpapan]], [[Indonesia]] after the ship's anchor was dropped in a prohibited area. The dragging anchor struck and ruptured the pipe. [https://splash247.com/captain-bulker-sparked-huge-indonesian-oil-spill-faces-lengthy-jail-sentence/ (Splash)]
;International relations
*[[April 2018 inter-Korean summit|2018 inter-Korean summit]], [[Panmunjom Declaration]]
**[[South Korea]]n [[President of South Korea|President]] [[Moon Jae-in]] meets [[North Korea]]n [[Supreme Leader (North Korean title)|leader]] [[Kim Jong Un]]. Moon and Kim agree to officially end the [[Korean War]] and the [[Korean conflict]] overall. Kim becomes the first North Korean leader to cross the [[Korean Demilitarized Zone]] since the war. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-southkorea-summit-crossing/kim-becomes-first-north-korean-leader-to-cross-border-into-south-since-war-idUSKBN1HY01L (Reuters)], [http://www.israelnationalnews.com/News/News.aspx/245065 (Israel National News)], [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/27/asia/korean-summit-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Germany–United States relations]]
**[[Chancellor of Germany|German Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] and [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] hold a joint press conference at the [[White House]]. Merkel states she believes that there can be a bilateral trade deal between the European Union and the United States. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-germany-trade/germanys-merkel-says-she-could-see-a-bilateral-eu-u-s-trade-deal-idUSKBN1HY2PQ (Reuters)] [https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2018/04/27/Watch-live-Trump-Germanys-Merkel-hold-joint-news-conference/3601524848936/?spt=rrs&or=6 (UPI)] 
*[[China–India relations]]
**Indian Prime Minister [[Narendra Modi]] invites [[President of China|Chinese President]] [[Xi Jinping]] to an informal summit next year as he began an ice-breaking visit to China on Friday in which the giant neighbors are seeking to re-set troubled ties. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-india/indias-modi-to-get-museum-tour-dinner-with-xi-as-china-trip-begins-idUSKBN1HY0LI (Reuters)]
;Law and crime
*[[Environmental policy of the European Union]]
**The [[European Union]] approves a total ban on [[neonicotinoid]]s,suspected of harming bees, which is expected to come into force by the end of 2018. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2018/apr/27/eu-agrees-total-ban-on-bee-harming-pesticides (''The Guardian'')] 
*[[Stoneman Douglas High School shooting]]
**[[Stoneman Douglas High School shooting#Suspect|Nikolas Cruz]], the accused suspect of the shooting at [[Stoneman Douglas High School]], is due to be in court. The hearing is expected to deal with several procedural issues, possibly including the setting of an initial trial date. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/nikolas-cruz-parkland-high-school-shooting-suspect-due-back-court-n869526 (NBC News)]
*[[North Korea–United States relations]], [[Crime in North Korea]]
**Fred and Cindy Warmbier, the parents of detained American student [[Otto Warmbier]], files a lawsuit against [[North Korea]] government, stating that Otto was "tortured and murdered", and also claimed that the DPRK "intentionally destroyed" their son's life. [https://www.smh.com.au/world/north-america/otto-warmbier-s-parents-sue-north-korea-over-his-torture-and-murder-20180427-p4zbxw.html (''The&nbsp;Sydney Morning Herald'')]
*[[Cyberwarfare]]
**[[Europol]] announces a coalition comprised of seven [[Europe]]an nations and the [[United States]] this week launched a [[cyberattack]] against [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] propaganda websites, taking a number of them down. [https://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/islamic-state-europol-amaq-shutdown_uk_5ae2e84ee4b04aa23f21f616 (The Huffington Post)]
*A man with a knife kills seven children and wounds twelve more in [[Mizhi]], [[Shaanxi]], [[China]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/04/knife-attacker-kills-children-wounds-19-china-180427130428508.html (al-Jazeera)]
*[[Terrorism in Iraq]]
**[[ISIL|Islamic State]] releases a video showing the shooting executions of two men, said to be election "advocators" from [[al-Tarmiyah]], [[Iraq]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-security-islamic-state/islamic-state-releases-video-showing-execution-of-iraq-election-advocators-idUSKBN1HY30O (Reuters)]
;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of Romania]]
**[[Romania]]n [[President of Romania|President]] [[Klaus Iohannis]] asks [[Prime Minister of Romania|Prime Minister]] [[Viorica Dăncilă]] to resign. Iohannis says Dăncilă did not consult him before endorsing a plan to move Romania's embassy in [[Israel]] to [[Jerusalem]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/04/romania-president-pm-israel-embassy-move-180427095228699.html (al-Jazeera)]
;Science and technology
*[[2017 Pohang earthquake]]
**Scientific studies have offered evidence that a geothermal plant may have caused the earthquake in [[South Korea]]. [https://phys.org/news/2018-04-evidence-geothermal-pohang-earthquake.amp (Phys.org)]
*[[Astrophysics]]
**A photograph from the [[Hubble Space Telescope]] reveals a companion star that survived the explosion of a [[supernova]] in galaxy [[NGC 7424]]. This brings strong evidence to a theory according to which [[Type_II_supernova#Type_IIb_supernovae|Type IIb "stripped-envelope" supernovae]] are due to stellar companions capturing hydrogen from the progenitor star's envelope before its explosion. [https://www.upi.com/Science_News/2018/04/27/Hubble-spots-surviving-companion-to-supernova-17-years-later/3291524836842/ (UPI)]
*[[De-extinction]]
**Biologists at the [[University of Melbourne]] announce plans to clone the extinct [[thylacine]] (Tasmanian tiger). [http://www.news.com.au/technology/science/animals/not-science-fiction-any-more-the-tasmanian-tiger-could-soon-be-back-from-extinction/news-story/b26dcb89e8c28f1232b5153e2c2c07e7 (News Corp Australia)]
*[[Detached object]]s
**Astronomers from the [[Outer Solar System Origins Survey]] (OSSOS) announce the discovery of ~{{convert|80|km|mi|adj=on}} asteroid {{mp|2015 KE|172}}, a detached object orbiting 44–222 times the distance from Earth to the Sun. [https://www.minorplanetcenter.net/mpec/K18/K18H97.html (Minor Planet Center)]
;Sports
*[[FIFA]] hands a lifetime ban to [[Marco Polo del Nero]], President of the [[Brazil]]ian [[Brazilian Football Confederation|Football Confederation]], for taking bribes. He is also fined one million [[Swiss franc]]s. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43925205 (BBC)]
*[[European Athletics Indoor Championships]]
**The city of [[Toruń]] in [[Poland]] wins the right to host the 2021 [[European Athletics Indoor Championships]], defeating [[Apeldoorn]] in the [[Netherlands]]. [http://www.thenews.pl/1/5/Artykul/361050,Poland%E2%80%99s-Torun-to-host-2021-European-Athletics-Indoor-Championships (Radio Poland)]
